name: SEN55 environmental sensor node
description: Sensirion all-in-one air quality module: particulate matter PM1.0/PM2.5/PM4.0/PM10 (0–1000 µg/m³, laser scattering with a built-in fan), relative humidity, temperature, VOC Index and NOx Index (1–500), a new reading every second. Runs on 4.5–5.5 V; I2C only (SEL to GND) at address 0x69, 100 kHz, 3.3 V logic levels. Sold as: Sensirion SEN55-SDN-T with a 6-wire JST GHR-06V cable (e.g. Sensirion SEN5x jumper cable or Adafruit's SEN5x cable), connector pins VDD, GND, SDA, SCL, SEL, NC; no pull-up resistors on the sensor.
eli5: A small box with a fan that sniffs the air and tells you how much dust, smoke-like gases and nitrogen oxides are in it, plus the temperature and humidity.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 5 V ± 10 % (4.5–5.5 V); about 70 mA while measuring (100 mA max in the first 60 s, 110 mA peaks)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (internally connected to the metal shield)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, open-drain, LVTTL 3.3 V compatible (5.5 V max). Needs an external pull-up (10 kΩ) to 3.3 V

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, open-drain, LVTTL 3.3 V compatible (5.5 V max). Needs an external pull-up (10 kΩ) to 3.3 V

pins.name: SEL
pins.description: Interface select: connect to GND (before or at power-up) to select I2C

buildNotes: Power VDD from 5 V (4.5–5.5 V); the fan and laser do not run on 3.3 V. Budget 100 mA during the first 60 s of measurement.
The sensor's connector is a 1.25 mm ACES 51451-0060N-001; use a JST GHR-06V-S cable (pin 1 VDD, 2 GND, 3 SDA, 4 SCL, 5 SEL, 6 NC) to reach the breadboard.
SEL (pin 5) must be tied to GND before or at power-up so the sensor selects I2C. Leave pin 6 unconnected.

SDA and SCL are open-drain and the sensor has no pull-ups: fit 10 kΩ resistors from SDA and from SCL to the board's 3.3 V (not 5 V, which would overdrive ESP32/Pico pins). The inputs accept 3.3 V logic (VIH 2.31 V).
I2C is limited to 100 kHz (standard mode) and the datasheet asks for connections under 10 cm or shielded cable.

Start Measurement is pointer 0x0021 (no data); poll 0x0202 for data ready, then write 0x03C4, wait 20 ms and read 24 bytes: eight big-endian 16-bit words, each followed by a CRC-8 (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). PM = uint16/10 µg/m³, RH = int16/100 %, T = int16/200 °C, VOC and NOx Index = int16/10; 0xFFFF (or 0x7FFF) means not yet known.
The NOx Index is unknown for about the first 10 s and the VOC/NOx indices need minutes to settle after start; PM readings settle after about 30 s.
Keep the metal shield floating: it is connected to GND inside the sensor.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sen55 import SEN55

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = SEN55(i2c)
sensor.start()

def f(v, fmt):
    return '--' if v is None else fmt % v

while True:
    m = sensor.read()
    print('PM1.0=%s PM2.5=%s PM10=%s ug/m3' % (f(m['pm1_0'], '%.1f'), f(m['pm2_5'], '%.1f'), f(m['pm10'], '%.1f')))
    print('RH=%s%% T=%sC VOC=%s NOx=%s' % (f(m['humidity'], '%.2f'), f(m['temperature'], '%.2f'), f(m['voc_index'], '%.0f'), f(m['nox_index'], '%.0f')))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the PM, humidity, temperature, VOC and NOx values set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (1 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
